the bundle is split rather than served whole: a 115 KB fleet index, 137 per-race chunks and 333 per-stage chunks, so a reader fetches a race's detail only on asking for that race. The UI suite asserts the same from the browser: two indexes and one stage chunk on first paint.

clauses.clause: Existing visual identity preserved, not replaced
clauses.detail: design judgement, and deliberately ungraded: whether the existing identity survived a change is a comparison against what it looked like before, which this bundle does not hold. The UI suite pins the parts that can be pinned — contrast ratios and reduced-motion behaviour — so a redesign cannot quietly fail those while the question of resemblance stays open.

clauses.clause: Route, profile and climb experience is modern and legible
clauses.detail: design judgement. Legibility is graded mechanically only where it reduces to contrast, which the UI suite checks for body, heading, table-cell, caption and race-held text in both themes; whether the route, profile and climb views are good is not something a script should claim to know.

half checked, half judgement, and the halves are named rather than averaged. Checked: every chart carries an aria-label, prefers-reduced-motion disables transitions, and all five text roles meet WCAG AA contrast in light and dark. Not checked: whether a chart's encoding is honest to the quantity it draws, which is a claim about meaning.
